items.title: 68002_Benny Waters oral history interview
items.q: And Sweets Edison and all them guys, [I] see all of them nowadays.

ctx.x: How often did you see your friends from the States in Europe, and to what extent did you remain in contact through writing with people who didn't come over to Europe? How much did you stay in touch with the old scene?

Well, I didn't stay in touch. Well, that's, like I said before, that's a big fault of mine, my staying in touch with people. I mean that's something I've got to, even at my age now I've still got to learn. But I saw a few American musicians [ ] - not as many as now, which is the last few years, I mean I can see everybody (PS laughs) 'cause everybody's come to Europe. I've seen Buddy Tate so often you'd think he's home when he's (PS laughs) - see Lockjaw all the, I saw Lockjaw in Paris, I saw Lockjaw in Denmark, I…
